Maybe you've done years of CBT or EMDR and you still freeze up or blow up at the same old triggers. Standard therapy is trying to rewrite the "code" (your thoughts and behaviors), while the "motherboard" (the brain's physical structure and chemistry) is often overheating or damaged, and code doesn't run well on a motherboard like that. This protocol goes after four specific neuro-biological problems that must be addressed before psychological tools can do much.

As we grow up, the "Role-Self" (the personality built to please and manage the people around us) gets locked in by Dopamine and DeltaFosB, and often your addiction is just what keeps that Role-Self running. The protocol targets the chemistry that holds the false persona in place, so the person you were before the trauma (your "True-Self") can come back out.

Neurological De-Armoring fixes the underpinnings first. Ketones (BHB) block HDAC, an enzyme that keeps genes switched off, and with Glutamate modulation on top, the protocol acts as a metabolic solvent that softens the "concrete" in the brainstem. Then we can dig under the house and pour a new foundation, and only after that update the psychological software upstairs.

The Anti-Breakthrough (Micro-Dosing): Long therapy sessions that leave you wrecked for days aren't doing what they're supposed to. Dr. Perry found the "therapeutic window" for a dysregulated brain is often only seconds long, and a sensitized, armored nervous system just can't take in sixty minutes of trauma processing, so the "hour-long breakthrough" has to wait.

So the goal is Micro-Dosing Safety: 30 seconds of regulated breathing, twenty times a day. It's more like physical therapy for a broken nervous system than running a marathon, and how often you do it matters more than how hard.

The Signal Dial (GluD Receptors): There's also a second dial. Johns Hopkins researchers have recently discovered that the brain uses GluD receptors like a master volume knob: NMDA is the spark, and GluD sets the baseline "hum" of the synapse. In an armored state, this dial is often jammed, either on "High" (Cerebellar Ataxia/Hyper-vigilance) or on "Low" (Apathy/Schizotypy).

The Repair (Leucine/L-Serine): L-Serine is what the brain makes D-Serine from, so it can help recalibrate the GluD "Volume Dial" and make therapy sessions that end with low fear and a sense of mastery stick better. The conversion is inefficient, though, which is why some people take D-serine itself, with a higher risk and a higher benefit. Leucine helps with structural repair and at the same time tunes synaptic gain, which eases the "itchy brain" feeling.

The Governor (Agmatine): If your Glutamate Storm is the hot, itchy, reactive, pain-y, rumination-heavy kind, agmatine is the optional "voltage governor." It may help when the problem isn't just excess glutamate in the synapse but NMDA/GluN2B over-reactivity, and it's a brake for that state, to use when you're in it, not a daily foundation nutrient.

Important conflict: don't take agmatine in the same session as D-Serine/DCS-style exposure or EMDR work, because agmatine partly brakes NMDA activity, which is the very learning and memory updating those tools are there to support. Use agmatine for storm control, and not right before a session where the goal is deliberate reconsolidation.
